input:
Our suspend-to-RAM (STR) resume is taking 3x longer than expected. The target is 200ms from resume trigger to display-on, but we're measuring 620ms. The resume path seems to have long delays in device driver resume callbacks.

ftrace suspend_resume + device_pm_callback:
  suspend_resume: resume_noirq start
    dpm_run_callback: pmic_i2c resume_noirq -> 2.1ms
    dpm_run_callback: mmc0 resume_noirq -> 5.3ms
    dpm_run_callback: usb0 resume_noirq -> 1.2ms
  suspend_resume: resume_noirq end (12ms)

  suspend_resume: resume_early start
    dpm_run_callback: clk_provider resume_early -> 45.2ms  <-- PLL relock
    dpm_run_callback: ddr_controller resume_early -> 82.1ms  <-- DDR retrain!
    dpm_run_callback: gpu resume_early -> 3.1ms
  suspend_resume: resume_early end (145ms)

  suspend_resume: resume start
    dpm_run_callback: display resume -> 180.3ms  <-- panel init sequence
    dpm_run_callback: camera resume -> 95.2ms  <-- why is camera resuming?
    dpm_run_callback: wifi resume -> 42.1ms
    dpm_run_callback: bluetooth resume -> 38.5ms
  suspend_resume: resume end (412ms)

Total resume: 12 + 145 + 412 = 569ms (+ 51ms kernel overhead = 620ms)

Key suspects: DDR retrain (82ms), display panel init (180ms), and camera resume (95ms) when camera app isn't even running. How do we get this under 200ms?
